Hon'ble Prashant Kumar,J.
1.

Heard Shri Ankit Kumar Pal, learned counsel for the applicant, Shri M.L. Jain, learned counsel appearing on behalf of opposite party no. 2, Shri Shashi Dhar Pandey, learned AGA for the State and perused the records.

2. The instant application under Section 482 CrPC has been filed by the applicant praying to quash the order dated 30.07.2016 passed by Special Judge, D.A.A., Agra in Criminal Revision No. 39/2016 in Complaint Case No. 2000/2015 (Smt. Sweta Gupta v. State of UP & Ors.) under Sections 323,
406, 504 IPC, P.S.- New Agra, District- Agra pending in the court of ACJM, Court No. 6, Agra and also prayed to further consider the case of the applicant and pass a fresh order in Criminal Revision No. 39/2016.
3.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that there is a matrimonial dispute.
The applicant was married to opposite party no. 2- Anurag Gupta on 09.07.2011.

Thereafter, on 17.02.2014, an FIR was lodged, in which, it was alleged that the husband of the applicant namely Anurag Gupta and other family members including his parents were asking for additional dowry of Rs. 10/- lakhs,
ornaments, house/flat and furniture.
It was further alleged in the FIR that because of the dowry demand, she had to face a lot of physical and mental agony.

The further allegation in the FIR is that the elder sister of the husband Niharika and the younger sister of the husband along with others also Smt.Sweta Gupta vs State Of U.P.And 8 Others on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103868454/
1 started asking for dowry and on 16.2.2014, they slapped her, kicked her and threw her out of the house.

sentences.text: During the course of the investigation, the statement was recorded and charge-sheet was filed on 27.05.2014 against opposite party nos. 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6.
In this, summons were issued and the trial is still going on.

4. During the pendency of this proceeding, the applicant had filed a complaint under Sections 323,
506, 420, 406, 120-B IPC, in which, allegation of dowry was made and alleged that Stridhan of the applicant was held back by opposite party no. 2.
Thereafter, a notice has been sent and when the same was returned, the instant complaint was filed.

After that, on 25.08.2015 statement under Section 200 CrPC was recorded, in which, it was alleged that family members of the husband had beaten her up and tied her with the rope on 16.02.2014, gave her electric shocks, slapped her, kicked her and threw her out of the house.
She further states that her father had gone there and lodged an FIR in the police station- Vijay Nagar.

Thereafter, on 26.09.2015, statement of witness namely Ashok Kumar (father of the applicant) was recorded, in which, he verbatim copied the contents of the FIR dated 17.02.2014 and on 07.09.2015, statement of witness namely Shailendra Varshneya (brother of the applicant) was recorded.
Thereafter, the opposite party no. 2 was summoned vide summoning order dated 18.11.2015.

This order was challenged by the opposite party no. 2 by means of Criminal Revision No. 39/2016, in which, the court below allowed the revision and summoning order dated 18.11.2015 was set aside and the report was called for the FIR pending the Police Station- Vijay Nagar and directed that the order under Section 210 CrPC may be passed.
This order has been challenged by the applicant by means of the instant application.

5. Per contra, Shri Murari Lal Jain, learned counsel appearing for opposite party no. 2 submits that as per the complaint, the opposite party no. 2 are staying with separately and further submits that the Stridhan is in the joint locker and keys of the joint locker is with the applicant.
He further submits that the applicant is filing various cases in various courts just to put undue pressure.

The list of these are as under :
"(i) Case Crime No. 46 of 2014, under Sections 498-A, 323, 506 IPC and Sections 3/4 of D.P. Act, Police Station- Mahila Thana, District- Ghaziabad.
(ii) NCR dated 05.11.2018 bearing NCR No. 0106 of 2018, under Sections 504, 506 IPC, Police Station- Hathras Kotwali, District- Hathras.
(iii) Case No. 11581 of 2022 (complaint case) [Sweta Gupta v. Anurag Gupta], under Sections 307, 504, 506, 427 IPC, District- Kasganj.
(iv) Case Crime No. 136 of 2017, under Sections 307, 504, 506 IPC, Police Station- G.R.P., District- Agra.
(v) Complaint Case No. 402 of 2014, under Section 12 of D.V. Act, District- Agra.
(vi) Case No. 294 of 2015, under Section 125 CrPC, Family Court, Agra."

sentences.text: He further submits that the applicant is trying to rope all the family members in litigation and wrecking vengeance against the husband.

He further submits that as per Section 210 CrPC, a complaint case cannot be entertained firstly when the police investigation for the same is being pending and both the FIR as well as criminal case is arising out of an alleged incident dated 16.02.2014.

Even in the complaint as well as in the FIR, only bald and general allegation has been levelled against the family members and specially those family members who are not staying with the applicant and had no connection with the applicant.
7. To buttress his arguments, he is placing reliance upon a judgement passed by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the matter of Geeta Mehrotra & Anr v. State Of U.P. & Anr, reported in 2012 (10) SCC 741.

entities.text: Geeta Mehrotra & Anr v. State Of U.P. & Anr, reported in 2012 (10) SCC 741
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. Shri Ankit Kumar Pal, learned counsel for applicant submits that the earlier cases filed by the applicant were different and this case is only for the Stridhan of the applicant which the opposite party no. 2 is illegally holding.

9. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the records.
10.
A bare perusal of the documents shows that initially, an FIR was lodged on 17.02.2014 for the incident which took place on 16.02.2014.

In the FIR, it is stated that the applicant was slapped,
kicked and thrown out of the house and only in her statement, she had tried to improve the case by alleging that she was beaten up by all the family member and was also electrocuted.
11.

Prima facie reading of the FIR as well as the complaint, the allegations levelled against the other family members are general in nature apart from the husband and has been only made just to harass the husband's family and just to put undue pressure.
The entire family members have been roped in and no specific allegation had been against them.

12. In Geeta Mehrotra & Anr v. State Of U.P. & Anr (supra), the Hon'ble Supreme Court emphasized the importance of scrutinizing the nature of allegations made against family members in matrimonial disputes.

entities.text: Geeta Mehrotra & Anr v. State Of U.P. & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Preeti Gupta Vs. State of Jharkhand (2010) 7 SCC 667, the Supreme Court highlighted the tendency to implicate not only the husband but also his immediate relations in complaints filed under Section 498A IPC.

entities.text: Preeti Gupta Vs. State of Jharkhand (2010) 7 SCC 667
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: These judgments underscore the need for courts to exercise caution and circumspection while dealing with such complaints, particularly in cases where allegations against distant relatives lack specificity or are based on general and omnibus assertions.

13. In the present case, a meticulous examination of the FIR and the subsequent complaint reveals that the allegations against the family members of the husband, apart from the husband himself, are general in nature.

The applicant's attempt to expand the scope of the litigation by implicating all family members later in her statement, even those with no direct involvement in the alleged incident, appears to be aimed at exerting undue pressure and harassing the husband's family.

14. Furthermore, as per the principles laid down in Neelu Chopra Vs. Bharti (2009) 10 SCC 184,
merely mentioning statutory provisions and lodging a complaint is not sufficient.
The particulars of the offence committed by each accused and their role in its commission must be clearly delineated.

Smt.Sweta Gupta vs State Of U.P.And 8 Others on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103868454/

entities.text: Sweta Gupta vs State Of U.P.And 8 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
However, in the present case, no specific allegations have been made against the family members,
and they have been roped in without any substantive basis.
15.
It shows that the applicant had lodged as many as six cases against the opposite party no. 2.

It also shows the conduct of the applicant as to how she is misusing/abusing the process of law just to wreck personal vendetta against the husband and his family members.
16.
As far as the impugned order is concerned, I see no illegality in the impugned order.
There was already a proceeding pending before the investigating officer and there was no need for the applicant to initiate a fresh complaint.
17. Accordingly, the instant application is dismissed.
